---
title: "Exploratory: funnels over follow-up time with rest-of-registry comparators (`r paste(params$models, collapse = ', ')`)"
author: "Naomi Loughlin"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date())`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: hide
params:
  data_dir: "../regitry-outlier-detection/outputs/UKA"   # regextract outputs (2025 reports)
  procedure: "UKA"
  models: ["Oxford"]          # brand from config/device_families.csv (detail level 1)
  attribute_source: "design"
  core_years: [1, 3, 5, 10]   # years every registry reports: trajectories, classification, funnels
  late_interval: [5, 10]      # interval used for the "late" flag
  k_reg_min: 3                # registries needed for a t-based pooled CI
  max_unsubtracted: 0.10      # drop a registry-year comparator if model rows without an estimate are > 10% of the rest
  n_sim: 20000                # simulations for the false-alarm rates
  out_dir: "figures"
  table_dir: "tables"
  save_png: true
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
for (f in list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
P <- params
MODELS <- unlist(P$models)
M1 <- MODELS[1]
SLUG <- paste0("fot_", tolower(P$procedure), "_", paste(tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", MODELS)), collapse = "_"))
CORE <- unlist(P$core_years)
LATE <- unlist(P$late_interval)
Z95 <- qnorm(0.975); Z998 <- qnorm(0.999)
f2 <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "f")
hr_txt <- function(r, d = 2) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", f2(r$hr, d), f2(r$hr_lcl, d), f2(r$hr_ucl, d))
save_fig <- function(p, name, width = 11, height = 6) if (isTRUE(P$save_png)) save_plot(p, paste0(SLUG, "_", name), P$out_dir, width, height)
dir.create(P$table_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
reg_scale <- function(regs, ...) scale_colour_manual(values = registry_colour(sort(unique(regs))), name = "Registry", ...)
```

```{r data}
ext <- load_extraction(P$data_dir, P$procedure)
ov_path <- "config/registry_means_override.csv"
overrides <- if (file.exists(ov_path)) readr::read_csv(ov_path, comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
inp <- crr_inputs(ext$device, load_families("config/device_families.csv"),
                  load_attribute_rules("config/device_attributes.csv"), MODELS, P$attribute_source)
YEARS <- sort(unique(inp$time_yr))
comp_all <- ft_comparators(ext$device, ext$casemix, inp, YEARS, overrides, P$max_unsubtracted)
comp <- filter(comp_all, comparator_ok)

cv <- ft_contrasts(inp, comp)                     # variant rows x year
br <- ft_brand_contrasts(inp, comp)               # brand (all rows of a registry collapsed) x year
cuts <- sort(unique(c(CORE, YEARS[YEARS > max(CORE)])))
iv_br <- ft_intervals(br, cuts)
iv_cv <- ft_intervals(cv, cuts)

# per-year pooling of the variant contrasts (shared comparator within registry in V)
pool_year <- purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(cv$time_yr)), function(t) {
  d <- filter(cv, time_yr == t); r <- ft_pool(d, P$k_reg_min, ft_V_year(d))
  if (is.null(r)) NULL else mutate(r, time_yr = t, .before = 1)
})
# per-interval pooling (the rest-of-registry part of the variance is shared within registry)
pool_int <- purrr::map_dfr(split(iv_cv, iv_cv$interval), function(d) {
  d <- mutate(d, v_rest_y = var_dH_r / dH_r^2)
  r <- ft_pool(d, P$k_reg_min, ft_V_year(d))
  if (is.null(r)) NULL else mutate(r, interval = d$interval[1], t1 = d$t1[1], t2 = d$t2[1], .before = 1)
}) |> arrange(t1)
jm <- ft_joint(cv)
joint_pred <- ft_joint_predict(jm, seq(1, max(cv$time_yr), by = 0.25))
joint_at <- ft_joint_predict(jm, sort(unique(cv$time_yr)))
jcf <- coef(summary(jm$fit))

# trajectory classification
late_lab <- paste0(LATE[1], "–", LATE[2], " y")
classify_lines <- function(cum, ints) {
  cum |>
    group_by(level, registry, row_id, label) |>
    group_modify(function(d, k) {
      zy <- setNames(d$z, d$time_yr)
      zl <- filter(ints, row_id == k$row_id, t1 == LATE[1], t2 == LATE[2])$z
      zl <- if (length(zl)) zl else NA_real_
      tibble::tibble(n = max(d$n_total), z_late = zl, pattern = ft_classify(zy, zl, CORE, Z95, Z998),
                     !!!setNames(as.list(zy[as.character(CORE)]), paste0("z_", CORE, "y")))
    }) |> ungroup()
}
cls_br <- classify_lines(br, iv_br)
cls_cv <- classify_lines(cv, iv_cv)
readr::write_csv(bind_rows(cls_br, cls_cv), file.path(P$table_dir, paste0(SLUG, "_trajectory_classification.csv")))

# false-alarm rates of the rules (brand-level lines; correlation of z across core years)
fa <- purrr::map_dfr(split(filter(br, time_yr %in% CORE), filter(br, time_yr %in% CORE)$registry), function(d) {
  d <- arrange(d, time_yr)
  if (nrow(d) < length(CORE)) return(NULL)
  C <- crr_row_cov(d$estimate, d$vi) + crr_row_cov(d$crr_rest, d$v_rest_y)
  R <- cov2cor(C)
  tibble::tibble(registry = d$registry[1], !!!as.list(ft_false_alarm(R, CORE, P$n_sim)),
                 corr_1_10 = R[1, ncol(R)], corr_5_10 = R[3, 4])
})

# numbers for the text
py <- function(t) filter(pool_year, time_yr == t)
pi_ <- function(lab) filter(pool_int, interval == lab)
b_lt <- jcf["lt", ]; b_0 <- jcf["intrcpt", ]
```

# Executive summary

> **Exploratory report.** The main funnel-over-time analysis is `funnel_trajectories.Rmd`, which keeps the overall registry mean and the funnel limits of `funnel_plots.Rmd`. This file is kept for the ideas it tests: rest-of-registry comparators, interval hazard ratios, pooling across registries, a joint model across years and the false-alarm simulation.

**What this file does.** The funnel plots compare each model with its own registry, which removes differences between registries: patients, revision thresholds, and how revision is defined. But a funnel looks at one follow-up year at a time. This report keeps the within-registry comparison and adds the time and cross-registry elements of Combescure et al. (2025, [doi:10.1530/EOR-2024-0020](https://doi.org/10.1530/EOR-2024-0020)). The aim is to see how the model's revision rate *relative to its own registry* changes over follow-up, and whether that pattern is consistent across registries. It is applied to `r M1` in `r n_distinct(cv$registry)` registries (`r paste(sort(unique(cv$registry)), collapse = ", ")`; 2025 reports).

**Methods in brief.**

1. **The funnel's comparison, made comparable across years.** For each registry row (variant) of the model and each follow-up year, the model's published CRR is compared with the **rest of the same registry** (registry CRR with the model's own procedures subtracted). The comparison is made on the complementary log–log scale: $\log \text{HR}(t) = \text{cloglog}(\text{CRR}_\text{model}) - \text{cloglog}(\text{CRR}_\text{rest})$, a log cumulative hazard ratio, with $z = \log\text{HR}/\text{SE}$. "Outside the 99.8% funnel" corresponds to $|z| > 3.09$, so this is the funnel test written as a number that can be followed over time.
2. **Funnels on one standardised scale.** Every registry is centred on its own rest-of-registry rate (HR = 1). All registries can therefore share **one funnel per year**, drawn with HR against precision.
3. **Z-score trajectories.** Each registry's brand-level line, and each variant, is followed over 1, 3, 5 and 10 years against fixed control lines at ±1.96 (95%) and ±3.09 (99.8%).
4. **Interval (conditional) hazard ratios.** These compare revision between consecutive years among knees still unrevised (0–1, 1–3, 3–5 and 5–10 years). They separate early failure from late failure, which cumulative rates blur together.
5. **Pooling across registries** (Combescure-style, on the relative scale). Per year and per interval: REML random effects with variants nested in registry, and a covariance term for variants of a registry that share the same comparator. Across years: one model with $\log\text{HR}(t) = \alpha + \beta\log t$ and registry- and variant-level random intercepts and slopes. Here $\alpha$ is the excess at 1 year and $\beta$ says whether it grows ($\beta > 0$) or fades ($\beta < 0$).
6. **Trajectory classification and false alarms.** Each line is labelled persistent / early / late / isolated, high or low. The false-alarm rate of each rule is estimated by simulation from the correlation between years.

**Outputs.**

- [Comparators](#comparators).
- [Standardised funnels per year](#funnels).
- [Z-trajectories](#trajectories) for brand and variants, at the core years and at all years.
- [Interval hazard ratios](#intervals).
- [Pooled HR over time](#pooled): per year, per interval, and the joint model.
- [Classification](#classification) and [false-alarm rates](#false-alarms).
- A [comparison with the 3-year funnel](#concordance).

Figures are written to `figures/`, named `r SLUG`_*.png. The classification table is written to `tables/`.

# Highlights

            paste(sprintf("%s: %s", cls_br$registry, tolower(cls_br$pattern)), collapse = "; ")))

                      if (length(pl)) paste(pl, collapse = ", ") else "none", if (length(pl) == 1) "is" else "are") }))

# Comparators: the rest of each registry {#comparators}

The funnels centre on the registry mean, which includes the model itself. That pulls the reference toward the model (self-masking), and here `r M1` is `r f2(100 * min(filter(comp, time_yr == 5)$model_share), 0)`–`r f2(100 * max(filter(comp, time_yr == 5)$model_share), 0)`% of each registry's UKAs. It also makes the model and the reference correlated. This report compares each model with the **rest of the registry**:

$$p_\text{rest}(t) = \frac{N\,p_\text{reg}(t) - \sum_i n_i\,p_i(t)}{N - \sum_i n_i}, \qquad \text{Var}(p_\text{rest}) \approx \text{Var}(p_\text{reg}) \frac{N}{N - \sum_i n_i}$$

- $\text{Var}(p_\text{reg})$ comes from the registry mean's published 95% CI. For AOANJRR it is published (Table KP18, all UKAs for osteoarthritis). For LROI (cemented + uncemented) it is pooled from the parts' CIs, as in `registry_means()`.
- It is put on the cloglog scale with the delta method.
- The model's rows and the rest of the registry are disjoint, so their errors are independent.
- **Dropped registry-years.** A registry-year is dropped when model rows without an estimate at that year make up more than `r f2(100 * P$max_unsubtracted, 0)`% of the "rest". In that case the comparator would still contain much of the model. Dropped: `r if (any(!comp_all$comparator_ok)) paste(sprintf("%s %s y", comp_all$registry[!comp_all$comparator_ok], comp_all$time_yr[!comp_all$comparator_ok]), collapse = ", ") else "none"`.

```{r comparators}
knitr::kable(comp_all |> filter(time_yr %in% c(CORE, 15)) |>
               transmute(Registry = registry, Year = time_yr, `Registry CRR %` = f2(100 * p_registry), `Registry n` = scales::comma(n_registry),
                         `Model share` = scales::percent(model_share, 1), `Rest-of-registry CRR %` = f2(crr_rest),
                         `SE (cloglog)` = f2(sqrt(v_rest_y), 3), Used = ifelse(comparator_ok, "yes", "no"), `Mean source` = mean_source),
             caption = "Registry mean, model share and rest-of-registry comparator at each follow-up year")
```

# Standardised funnels, one per year {#funnels}

On the HR scale every registry is centred on its own rest-of-registry rate (HR = 1). The control limits depend only on the estimate's precision: $\exp(\pm z/\text{precision})$, with precision = 1/SE. One funnel per year can therefore hold all registries, and points from different registries can be compared directly. Precision comes from the published KM CIs, which allow for censoring; the binomial n used in the main funnels does not.

```{r funnels, fig.height = 5.5}
fd <- bind_rows(mutate(filter(cv, time_yr %in% CORE), what = "Variant (registry row)"),
                mutate(filter(br, time_yr %in% CORE), what = "Brand (registry rows collapsed)")) |>
  mutate(prec = 1 / se, yr = factor(paste(time_yr, ifelse(time_yr == 1, "year", "years")), levels = paste(CORE, ifelse(CORE == 1, "year", "years"))),
         out = abs(z) > Z998)
pr <- range(fd$prec); xs <- exp(seq(log(pr[1] * 0.8), log(pr[2] * 1.2), length.out = 200))
lim <- tidyr::crossing(prec = xs, lev = c("95%", "99.8%")) |>
  mutate(zc = ifelse(lev == "95%", Z95, Z998), up = exp(zc / prec), lo = exp(-zc / prec))
pf <- ggplot(fd, aes(prec, hr)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = lim, aes(prec, up, linetype = lev), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_line(data = lim, aes(prec, lo, linetype = lev), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = registry, shape = what, size = what), alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(fd, out, what != "Variant (registry row)"), aes(label = registry, colour = registry),
                           size = 2.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`Variant (registry row)` = 16, `Brand (registry rows collapsed)` = 18), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`Variant (registry row)` = 1.8, `Brand (registry rows collapsed)` = 4), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = LEVEL_LINETYPES[c("95%", "99.8%")], name = "Control limit") +
  reg_scale(fd$registry) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 1, 1.5, 2, 3)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.3, 3.2)) +
  facet_wrap(~ yr, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Precision (1 / SE of log HR)", y = "HR vs rest of own registry (log scale)",
       title = sprintf("%s against the rest of its own registry: one standardised funnel per follow-up year", M1),
       subtitle = "Each registry is centred on its own rest-of-registry rate. Diamonds = brand per registry; dots = variants as listed.") +
  theme_funnel()
pf
save_fig(pf, "funnels_by_year", 13, 5.5)
```

# Z-score trajectories {#trajectories}

These show the funnel test across time: one line per registry (brand level) or per variant, with fixed control lines. A line above +1.96 is outside the 95% upper funnel at that year; above +3.09 it is outside the 99.8% upper funnel.

```{r traj-helpers}
traj_plot <- function(d, years, facet = FALSE, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  d <- filter(d, time_yr %in% years)
  zr <- max(4, ceiling(max(abs(d$z), na.rm = TRUE)))
  ggplot(d, aes(time_yr, z, colour = registry, group = row_id)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Z95, ymax = Z95, fill = "grey92") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-Z998, Z998), linetype = LEVEL_LINETYPES[["99.8%"]], colour = "grey35") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-Z95, Z95), linetype = LEVEL_LINETYPES[["95%"]], colour = "grey35") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    (if (!facet) ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = d |> group_by(row_id) |> slice_max(time_yr, n = 1),
                                          aes(label = registry), nudge_x = 0.4, hjust = 0, direction = "y",
                                          size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, segment.size = 0.2)) +
    (if (facet) facet_wrap(~ registry, nrow = 1)) +
    reg_scale(d$registry) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = years, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.12))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-zr, zr)) +
    labs(x = "Years since primary", y = "z (log HR vs rest of registry / SE)", title = title,
         subtitle = subtitle %||% "Shaded = within the 95% funnel; dashed = 95% limits (±1.96); solid = 99.8% limits (±3.09).") +
    theme_funnel()
}
```

```{r traj-brand, fig.height = 5.5}
p <- traj_plot(br, CORE, title = sprintf("%s, brand level per registry: z-score at each core year", M1)); p
save_fig(p, "z_trajectory_brand_core", 10, 5.5)
p <- traj_plot(br, sort(unique(br$time_yr)), title = sprintf("%s, brand level per registry: z-score at every year with a comparator", M1)); p
save_fig(p, "z_trajectory_brand_all", 11, 5.5)
```

```{r traj-variant, fig.height = 5}
cvl <- mutate(cv, row_id = row_id)
p <- traj_plot(cvl, CORE, facet = TRUE, title = sprintf("%s variants (registry rows): z-score at each core year", M1)) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(cvl, time_yr == max(CORE)), aes(label = gsub(" Partial Knee| / Oxford Partial Knee", "", label)),
                           size = 2.2, nudge_x = 1, hjust = 0, direction = "y", show.legend = FALSE, segment.size = 0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = CORE, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.9)))
p
save_fig(p, "z_trajectory_variants_core", 15, 5)
```

# Interval (conditional) hazard ratios {#intervals}

A cumulative HR at 10 years still carries the first-year revisions. An implant that does well early and badly late therefore shows only a slow drift. The interval HR compares revision *within* each interval among knees still unrevised at its start:

$$\Delta H = H(t_2) - H(t_1),\quad H = -\log(1 - \text{CRR}/100), \qquad \log\text{HR}_{[t_1,t_2]} = \log\frac{\Delta H_\text{model}}{\Delta H_\text{rest}}$$

- The variance comes from independent increments: $\text{Var}(\Delta H) \approx \text{Var}(H_2) - \text{Var}(H_1)$, with $\text{Var}(H) = v H^2$. When rounding of the published CIs makes that difference ≤ 0, $\text{Var}(H_2)\,\Delta H/H_2$ is used instead. Number of cells where that fallback was needed: `r sum(iv_br$var_approx_m | iv_br$var_approx_r)` (brand level) and `r sum(iv_cv$var_approx_m | iv_cv$var_approx_r)` (variant level).
- The conditional CRR of each interval is $1 - e^{-\Delta H}$.

```{r intervals, fig.height = 5.5}
ivp <- filter(iv_br, t2 <= max(CORE))
ilev <- unique(ivp$interval[order(ivp$t1)])
regs <- sort(unique(ivp$registry))
ivp <- mutate(ivp, x = match(interval, ilev) + (match(registry, regs) - (length(regs) + 1) / 2) * 0.11 - 0.08)
pint <- filter(pool_int, t2 <= max(CORE)) |> mutate(x = match(interval, ilev) + 0.32)
p <- ggplot(ivp, aes(x, hr, colour = registry)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = hr_lcl, ymax = hr_ucl), size = 0.35) +
  geom_errorbar(data = pint, aes(x = x, ymin = pi_lcl, ymax = pi_ucl), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(data = pint, aes(x = x, ymin = hr_lcl, ymax = hr_ucl), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.08) +
  geom_point(data = pint, aes(x = x, y = hr), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 22, fill = "black", size = 3.2) +
  reg_scale(ivp$registry) + scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 0.67, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(ilev), labels = ilev) +
  labs(x = "Follow-up interval", y = "Interval HR vs rest of registry (log scale)",
       title = sprintf("%s: revision within each interval among knees unrevised at its start, vs the rest of the registry", M1),
       subtitle = "Coloured = brand level per registry (95% CI). Black squares (right of each group) = pooled across registries; grey bars = 95% prediction interval.") +
  theme_funnel()
p
save_fig(p, "interval_hr", 11, 5.5)
knitr::kable(pool_int |> transmute(Interval = interval, Registries = k_reg, `Pooled HR (95% CI)` = hr_txt(cur_data()),
                                    `95% PI` = paste(f2(pi_lcl), "–", f2(pi_ucl)), `p` = format.pval(pval, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
                                    CI = ci_method, `σ²` = sigma2),
             caption = "Pooled interval HR vs rest of registry (variant rows, nested in registry)")
knitr::kable(iv_br |> filter(t2 <= max(CORE)) |> mutate(cell = sprintf("%s [%s%% vs %s%%]", hr_txt(cur_data()), f2(crr_cond_m, 1), f2(crr_cond_r, 1))) |>
               select(Registry = registry, interval, cell) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = interval, values_from = cell),
             caption = "Brand-level interval HR (95% CI) [conditional CRR: model vs rest of registry] per registry")
```

# Pooled HR over time {#pooled}

## Per year (Combescure-style, on the relative scale)

At each year, the variant log HRs are pooled with REML, random effects for registry and variant within registry, and t / containment-df CIs. Variants of one registry share the rest-of-registry comparator, so their sampling errors are correlated. This is entered as an off-diagonal covariance $\text{Var}(y_\text{rest})$ between them.

```{r pool-year}
knitr::kable(pool_year |> transmute(Year = time_yr, Registries = k_reg, k, `Pooled HR (95% CI)` = hr_txt(cur_data()),
                                     `95% PI` = paste(f2(pi_lcl), "–", f2(pi_ucl)), p = format.pval(pval, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
                                     `Q (p)` = sprintf("%s (%s)", f2(Q, 0), format.pval(Q_p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)), `σ²` = sigma2,
                                     CI = ci_method),
             caption = "Pooled HR vs rest of registry at each follow-up year (years with 2 registries: z CI, exploratory)")
readr::write_csv(pool_year, file.path(P$table_dir, paste0(SLUG, "_pooled_hr_by_year.csv")))
```

## One model across years

$$\log\text{HR}_{rj}(t) = \alpha + \beta \log t + (u_{0r} + u_{1r}\log t) + (w_{0rj} + w_{1rj}\log t) + \varepsilon_{rj}(t)$$

The sampling covariance $V$ has two parts within a registry:

- each variant's own covariance across years (independent increments, as in `crr_meta_analysis.Rmd`);
- the comparator's covariance across years, shared by all variants and years of that registry.

$e^\alpha$ is the HR at 1 year. $\beta$ is the change in log HR per unit of log t: $\beta < 0$ means the excess fades with follow-up, $\beta > 0$ means it grows (the late-failure signature).

```{r joint}
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(Term = c("α (log HR at 1 year)", "β (per unit log t)"),
                            Estimate = f2(jcf$estimate, 3), `95% CI` = paste(f2(jcf$ci.lb, 3), "–", f2(jcf$ci.ub, 3)),
                            df = jcf$df, p = format.pval(jcf$pval, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)),
             caption = sprintf("Joint model (k = %s estimates, %s variants; random %s per registry and variant; t / containment df)",
                               jm$fit$k, n_distinct(jm$data$row_id), if (jm$slopes) "intercepts and log t slopes" else "intercepts"))
```

```{r pooled-fig, fig.height = 6}
bo <- filter(br, time_yr %in% sort(unique(cv$time_yr)))
p <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(data = joint_pred, aes(time_yr, ymin = hr_lcl, ymax = hr_ucl), fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = joint_pred, aes(time_yr, hr), colour = "grey30", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = bo, aes(time_yr, hr, colour = registry), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = bo, aes(time_yr, hr, colour = registry), size = 1.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = pool_year, aes(time_yr, ymin = pi_lcl, ymax = pi_ucl), width = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 2.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = pool_year, aes(time_yr, ymin = hr_lcl, ymax = hr_ucl), width = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = pool_year, aes(time_yr, hr, fill = exploratory), shape = 22, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "white"), labels = c(`FALSE` = "Pooled (>= 3 registries)", `TRUE` = "Pooled, exploratory (2 registries)"), name = NULL) +
  reg_scale(bo$registry) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(cv$time_yr))) + scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 0.67, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Years since primary", y = "Cumulative HR vs rest of registry (log scale)",
       title = sprintf("%s relative to its own registry over follow-up: per registry and pooled", M1),
       subtitle = "Coloured = brand level per registry. Squares = per-year pooled HR (95% CI); grey bars = 95% prediction interval. Dashed = joint model (95% CI).") +
  theme_funnel()
p
save_fig(p, "pooled_hr_over_time", 11, 6)
```

# Trajectory classification {#classification}

The rules are applied to the core years (`r paste(CORE, collapse = ", ")`) and the late interval (`r late_lab`). The high side is described here; the low side mirrors it.

| Pattern | Rule | Typical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Persistent high | z > 1.96 at ≥ 2 consecutive core years | Sustained excess: strongest signal |
| Late high | `r late_lab` interval z > 1.96, without persistent high | Late failure (wear, loosening, disease progression) |
| Early high | z > 1.96 only at the first two core years | Early failure (technique, learning curve, early loosening or infection) |
| Isolated high | Any other single exceedance | Weak signal; watch |
| "(beyond 99.8%)" | Any z beyond ±3.09 in that direction | Also outside the 99.8% funnel |

```{r classification}
fmtz <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", f2(x, 1))
mk <- function(d) d |> transmute(Registry = registry, Line = label, n = scales::comma(n),
                                 !!!setNames(lapply(paste0("z_", CORE, "y"), function(cn) fmtz(d[[cn]])), paste0("z ", CORE, " y")),
                                 !!paste0("z ", late_lab) := fmtz(z_late), Pattern = pattern)
knitr::kable(mk(cls_br), caption = "Brand level (all rows of a registry collapsed): z at each core year, late-interval z, and pattern")
knitr::kable(mk(cls_cv), caption = "Variants (registry rows as listed)")
```

# False-alarm rates of the rules {#false-alarms}

The z-scores of one implant at different years share patients, so they are correlated. Rules that look across years need their own false-alarm rate. For each registry's brand-level line, z-trajectories under the null (true HR = 1 at every year) are simulated from that line's correlation matrix across the core years: the implant's own covariance plus the comparator's. Each rule's high-side flag rate is then counted. The late interval is treated as independent of the cumulative z's (independent increments).

```{r false-alarm}
knitr::kable(fa |> transmute(Registry = registry, `Corr(z1, z10)` = f2(corr_1_10), `Corr(z5, z10)` = f2(corr_5_10),
                             `5-year funnel alone` = scales::percent(single_year, 0.1), `Any core year` = scales::percent(any_year, 0.1),
                             `Persistent (2 consecutive)` = scales::percent(persistent, 0.1),
                             `Late interval (not persistent)` = scales::percent(late_interval, 0.1),
                             `Any rule` = scales::percent(any_rule, 0.1)),
             caption = "High-side flag rate under the null, 95% one-sided level per test (nominal 2.5% for one test)")
```

How to read the rates:

- **Flagging on any core year** roughly triples the false-alarm rate of a single funnel.
- **The persistence rule** stays at or below the single-funnel rate, because adjacent years are strongly correlated. It is the rule to use for a time-aware flag at the 95% level.
- **The late-interval flag** adds about one test's worth of false alarms, because it is close to independent of the cumulative years. Combining rules should therefore be done at a stricter level, for example 99.8% for the "any rule" combination.

# Comparison with the 3-year funnel {#concordance}

How the funnel framework and this report differ:

| | Main funnels | This report |
|---|---|---|
| Reference | Registry mean, including the model | Rest of the registry |
| Uncertainty | Binomial, from n | Published KM CIs |
| Scale | Difference in rates | Ratio (cloglog) |

The table shows both classifications at 3 years for each variant.

```{r concordance}
t3 <- filter(cv, time_yr == 3)
conc <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(t3)), function(i) {
  r <- t3[i, ]
  lim <- funnel_limits(r$p_registry, r$n_total, c(0.95, 0.998), "normal")
  p <- r$estimate / 100
  tibble::tibble(Registry = r$registry, Variant = r$label, n = scales::comma(r$n_total),
                 `Funnel (registry mean, binomial)` = case_when(p > lim$upper[lim$level == 0.998] ~ "above 99.8%", p > lim$upper[lim$level == 0.95] ~ "above 95%",
                                                                 p < lim$lower[lim$level == 0.998] ~ "below 99.8%", p < lim$lower[lim$level == 0.95] ~ "below 95%", TRUE ~ "within"),
                 `This report: z` = f2(r$z, 1),
                 `This report (rest of registry, KM CI)` = case_when(r$z > Z998 ~ "above 99.8%", r$z > Z95 ~ "above 95%", r$z < -Z998 ~ "below 99.8%", r$z < -Z95 ~ "below 95%", TRUE ~ "within"))
})
knitr::kable(conc, caption = "3-year classification: standard funnel vs rest-of-registry z")
```

Most classifications agree in direction. Where they differ, there are three reasons:

- **Self-masking.** Removing the model from its own reference moves the reference away from the model. For a brand that is 50–75% of a registry, as Oxford is in LROI and EPRD, this has a large effect.
- **KM CIs vs binomial.** Published KM CIs are wider than binomial limits once follow-up is censored.
- **Ratio vs difference scale.**

# Decisions {#decisions}

| Decision | Choice | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Comparator | Rest of the registry (registry mean minus the model's rows), not the registry mean | Removes self-masking and makes model and reference independent. The brand is a large share of every registry here. |
| Comparator variance | $\text{Var}(p_\text{reg})\,N/(N - n_\text{model})$ | Variance scales with 1/size. This is conservative compared with subtracting covariances, which can turn negative with rounded CIs. |
| Unusable comparators | Dropped when model rows without an estimate exceed `r f2(100 * P$max_unsubtracted, 0)`% of the rest | Otherwise the "rest" contains much of the model (e.g. NJR 20 y, LROI 16 y, AOANJRR 20 y). |
| Scale | Log cumulative HR (cloglog difference) | Same scale as `crr_meta_analysis.Rmd`. It removes multiplicative registry differences, which are interpretable as HRs under proportional hazards. |
| Uncertainty | Published KM 95% CIs (SE backed out on the cloglog scale) | Accounts for censoring, unlike binomial funnel limits. |
| Brand level per registry | The registry's rows weighted by procedures, as in detail level 1; SE from the rows' published CIs | This is the brand's rate in that registry. Inverse-variance weighting on the cloglog scale was not used: it weights rows by their number of revisions and would pull the brand rate toward high-revision variants. |
| Pooling | Variant rows nested in registry, shared-comparator covariance, t / containment df | As in `crr_meta_analysis.Rmd`, with the covariance needed because variants of a registry share one comparator. |
| Classification | 95% one-sided per test; persistent = 2 consecutive core years; late = `r late_lab` interval; "(beyond 99.8%)" tag | The persistence rule keeps the false-alarm rate near that of a single funnel (simulated). |
| Core years | `r paste(CORE, collapse = ", ")` | Reported by every registry, so trajectories are comparable. Other years are shown in the "all years" figure and used in the joint model. |

# Limitations {#limitations}

1. **The rest-of-registry rate treats KM estimates as additive**, i.e. a weighted average of the parts. It is approximate, and more so where censoring patterns differ between the model and the rest. Its variance is a scaling approximation.
2. **Comparator populations do not always match exactly.** The AOANJRR mean (KP18) is osteoarthritis only, while its model rows (KP17) include all diagnoses; KP18 covers 99.2% of KP17. The LROI means are the cemented and uncemented totals for osteoarthritis. The SIRIS "CH average" has no n, so the listed volume is used.
3. **Interval HRs depend on the published CI precision.** Var(ΔH) from the difference of two rounded variances is unstable for short intervals and small models. The fallback is noted where used.
4. **No model-specific case mix.** The rest-of-registry comparison removes registry-wide differences, but not differences in patients between the model and the other models in the same registry.
5. **Correlation approximations.** The within-row covariance across years and the false-alarm simulation use the independent-increments approximation. The late-interval z is assumed independent of the cumulative z's.
6. **Changing composition at long follow-up.** At 15–20 years only some variants and older cohorts remain. Brand-level lines at those years describe a different mix than at 1–5 years.
7. **Few registries.** With 5 registries, the pooled HRs and the between-registry variance are imprecise. Years with 2 registries are exploratory.

# Reference

Combescure C, Smith JA, Barea C, Hoogervorst LA, Nelissen R, Marang-van de Mheen PJ, Lübbeke A, and the Arthroplasty registry group. Cumulative risk of revision after primary total hip arthroplasty in registries internationally: systematic review and meta-analysis of selected hip stems and cups. *EFORT Open Reviews* 2025;10:277–285. doi:10.1530/EOR-2024-0020.
